summary.text: A 67-year-old woman with a family history of SLE and osteoporosis treated with calcium and vitamin D presented to rheumatology with migratory arthralgias and was referred to dermatology for a disseminated dermatosis of multiple pruritic wheals lasting more than 24 hours, present for eight months.

Skin biopsy showed a perivascular mixed infiltrate with neutrophils and eosinophils, nuclear dust and mild fibrinoid necrosis. Laboratory studies showed low C3 and C4, elevated CRP and TSH, ESR and glucose marked abnormal in the table, a weakly positive ANA at 1:100 and negative anti-Sm, anti-dsDNA, anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies; anti-C1q could not be assessed.

Hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis was diagnosed; SLE classification criteria were not met and SLE was considered unlikely. Prednisone 0.5 mg/kg per day with a weekly 5 mg taper led to near-complete remission of lesions within two months, and repeat rheumatology evaluation ruled out systemic involvement.

Subclinical hypothyroidism was identified and the patient was referred to endocrinology; quarterly dermatology and semiannual rheumatology and endocrinology follow-up with routine laboratory monitoring is planned.
